item.title: BIS residential property price statistics, Q4 2025
item.description: Real global house prices fell by 0.6% year on year (yoy) at the end of 2025. Real prices were almost stable in advanced economies (0.4% yoy), while they continued to decrease in emerging market economies (–1.4% yoy), especially in Asia. Since the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic, real global house prices have increased by almost 3%. Among major jurisdictions, Türkiye, Australia and Mexico recorded the strongest increases, while prices in China and Canada were still below their pre-pandemic levels. From a longer-term perspective, real global house prices have increased by almost 20% since the end of the Great Financial Crisis (GFC) of 2007–09. item.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued.
